document_summary: Rashad begins at Quran 7:12 with Satan's refusal to prostrate and develops an extensive premortal anthropology. The opening also recalls a Chicago religious seminar, physical evidence for the Quran, and the role of a human messenger. The central discussion argues that Adam and Eve initially existed outside visible earthly bodies, that eating from the tree exposed or transferred them into bodies already prepared on Earth, and that all souls had been created, judged, put to death, and assigned future bodies according to their premortal positions. Near-death experiences, natural instinct, jinn companions, spiritual witnesses, cloning, the soul's relation to intellect and memory, brain chemistry, organ transplantation, bodily hormones, death, and the sleepers of the cave are used to explore the distinction between soul, brain, and body.

Adam and Eve's invisible bodies, the tree, another dimension, and entry into earthly bodies
Rashad argues that Adam and Eve were initially outside visible earthly bodies. The command not to approach the tree preserved their state; when they broke the law, their bodies became visible and they were drawn or 'sucked' into prepared bodies on Earth. The group debates the Arabic wording concerning what had been hidden from them, whether this means part or all of the body, and whether Paradise existed in another dimension.
